Distribution. China (Hubei, Sichuan); Japan and Korea. Notes. The status of C. nipponensis has been changed several times. Originally, it was described as a variety of C. vittifrons (Sichel) when found by Uchida in Japan for its black head, darker wings, and the very small spots on T 3 in both sexes (Uchida 1933). Betrem (1941) treated it as a variety of C. fascinata Smith by displaying the differences between C. fascinata and C. vittifrons. Osten (2005) treated it as a subspecies of C. vittifrons again. We found a male from Sichuan province of China (IOZ) and a female from Hubei (RMNH) of C. nipponensis, both are different from the nominate C. vittifrons. We consider C. nipponensis a separate species because of the distinct carina present on the area between the antennal sockets (“ frontal spatium ”) in both sexes and the nearly completely dark integument of both sexes.
